title: Tests share the real on-disk books.db with no teardown, so they are order-dependent and leak state
evidence: test_app.py:5-12 — the `client` fixture calls `init_db()` (test_app.py:11) but never redirects the DB path and never drops/truncates the table; app.py:8 hard-codes `DATABASE = 'books.db'`. Every test run accumulates rows in the same file.
suggestion: Monkeypatch app.DATABASE to a tmp_path-scoped file (or use ':memory:' with a shared connection) in the fixture and delete it on teardown, so each test starts from a known empty table.

title: List/filter assertions use `len(data) >= 1`, which passes on leftover rows from earlier tests
evidence: test_app.py:73 (`assert len(data) >= 1`) in test_get_books and test_app.py:92-93 in test_get_books_by_author — neither asserts that the book created by that test is the one returned.
suggestion: Assert an exact count against a clean DB, or look the created id up in the returned list, so the ?author= filter is actually verified rather than satisfied by residue.

title: Bare `except Exception` collapses every write error into an opaque 500 and discards the exception
evidence: app.py:75, app.py:174, app.py:198 — each is `except Exception as e:` returning a generic message; `e` is bound but never logged or included.
suggestion: Catch sqlite3.IntegrityError/sqlite3.Error specifically, log the exception, and let unexpected errors surface rather than masking them as 500.

title: SQLite connections are closed on explicit paths only — an exception outside the try leaks the connection
evidence: app.py:51, 84, 111, 143, 181 each call `conn = get_db_connection()` and rely on hand-placed `conn.close()` rather than a context manager; e.g. app.py:92 `cursor.fetchall()` in get_books sits outside any try/finally.
suggestion: Use `with contextlib.closing(get_db_connection()) as conn:` or Flask's `g` + `teardown_appcontext` so the connection is released on every path.

title: init_db() runs only under `__main__`, so a WSGI/import-based deployment never creates the books table
evidence: app.py:202-204 — `init_db()` is called inside `if __name__ == '__main__':`; nothing at import time creates the schema. README.md:32 documents only `python app.py`, so the documented path works, but `flask run`/gunicorn would hit `no such table: books`.
suggestion: Call init_db() at import time (or from an app factory) so the schema exists regardless of how the app is started.

title: PUT /books/{id} is full-replace and silently nulls year/isbn when they are omitted
evidence: app.py:140-141 — `year = data.get('year')` / `isbn = data.get('isbn')` default to None, and app.py:156-157 writes them unconditionally, so a PUT sending only title+author erases year and isbn.
suggestion: Either document the full-replace contract in README.md or preserve existing values when a field is absent from the body.

title: requirements.txt omits pytest although README documents running the tests with it
evidence: requirements.txt contains only `Flask==2.3.3`; README.md:41 instructs `python -m pytest test_app.py -v`, and test_app.py:1 imports pytest.
suggestion: Add pytest to requirements.txt (or a requirements-dev.txt) so the documented test command works after a clean install.

title: Dev server starts with debug=True bound to 0.0.0.0
evidence: app.py:204 — `app.run(debug=True, host='0.0.0.0', port=5001)` exposes the Werkzeug debugger console on all interfaces.
suggestion: Default debug to False (or read it from an env var) and document a production WSGI command in README.md.

title: 11 tests delivered against a 3-test minimum, covering every route plus 404 and validation paths
evidence: test_app.py defines 11 `test_*` functions including test_create_book_missing_fields:41, test_book_not_found:171, test_update_nonexistent_book:178, test_delete_nonexistent_book:193.
